title: The largest reading, with NaN in the data

blocks.text: `NaN` ("not a number") is what a failed floating-point computation produces. Every relational operator with a `NaN` operand is `false`, even `NaN == NaN`, so the page's advice is to test for it with `Double.isNaN`. And beware of `Double.MIN_VALUE`: it is the smallest **positive** double, not the most negative one.

A sensor writes one `double` per reading, and writes `NaN` when a reading failed. Write `Readings.largest(double[] readings)`. It returns the largest real reading, ignoring every `NaN`. When there is no real reading (an empty array, or only `NaN`s) it returns `NaN`.

cases.says: It returns the largest of the readings.
When every reading is negative the largest is still negative, not Double.MIN_VALUE.
A NaN reading is skipped rather than spreading into the answer.
With no real reading the answer is NaN, not an infinity.
